core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage, Smarden
core.listing:
2 Forge Cottages is an end-of-terrace Victorian cottage built around 1880, constructed of red brick under a clay-tiled roof. The cottage stands within the Smarden Conservation Area.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. Ledged-and-braced doors are found throughout. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor and a range alcove; the beams in this room are reclaimed (1990s). 

On the first floor, bedroom one measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom two measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"). There is one bathroom. Head height at the top of the stairs is restricted to approx. 1.88m (6'2").

The rear cottage garden extends approx. 12m (40ft) and has a brick path and a timber shed. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded.

The village pub is approx. 2 minutes' walk.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. Construction: Standard – red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Electricity: mains. Water: mains (not metered). Sewerage: septic tank. Heating: oil-fired central heating. Broadband: FTTC. Mobile signal: good outdoors, variable indoors. Parking: on-street. Building safety: none known. The property is within the Smarden Conservation Area. The septic tank is shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. Coastal erosion: none known. Planning: none known. Accessibility: none known. Coalfield / mining: none known. The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. Restricted head height at top of stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2").
